# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say the schedule and subs not showing up are what beat the daily log, so one group named 'Keeping the schedule and subs showing up' is exactly how a super would sort them, and the name is plain.
whys.g2: There is no junk answer on this line; both answers are on-topic about what made other work more pressing than the log.

founder.order_why: Screen 4 (how far back to look) sits between two context screens with the same heading, so the context step feels split in two; the rest runs naturally from who and when, to the problem, to who gets asked.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the identical kicker and question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'), so they read as the same screen asked twice even if they collect different fields.
founder.missing: No screen asks how long the log takes. The hours in the trailer (up to 3 a day, 2+ hours for a final report) are the heart of the problem, and only how many supers and how many days are asked. Nothing asks who pays: the general contractor buys per site per month, not the superintendent. Nothing covers the scribe itself or the price (about $1k per site per month), so the flow never reaches the buyer side the Part 3 contractor operations leads would answer.

PRIMARY.order_why: Asking which part I'd most like made easier before asking how my last daily log actually went feels backwards, since I'd want to describe the last log first and then say what to fix.
PRIMARY.asked_twice: Screens 2 and 3 overlap: whether I logged my site walk photos and notes in the last 5 working days, then on how many days, which the second question alone would cover with a zero.
PRIMARY.missing: How long it takes to get the photos and notes into Procore or ACC each day, how many photos I'm handling, and whether I've had to pull those logs for a delay dispute or claim with the owner.

screens.why1: Right after picking who asks the questions, how my supers will answer is the obvious next thing to settle before the link goes out.
screens.why2: Short and plain: talk to Daphne on video, or read and tap, or let them pick -- I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I know my supers: they're in the truck or the trailer with a phone, and I can judge whether they'd rather tap or talk to a video.
screens.why4: Three distinct ways that cover the real choice, each described in words I'd use, and 'Let them choose' is the fair middle option.
screens.why5: Nothing of mine is changed; it asks about the format, and 'Read and tap' is what I picked.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how supers will answer, it's the obvious next step to say who actually receives the link, and it's the last screen before sending.
screens.why2: Each option is short and plain to me as a founder: my own contacts, a list from Keel's search, or one link posted where supers already gather.
screens.why3: I know who I'd reach: superintendents I've met driving around Napa, South Bay and SF, plus GC intros, so I can pick 'people I know by name' without guessing.
screens.why4: The three routes are distinct and cover how I'd reach supers (direct, searched, or a group link), and no escape is needed on a setup choice like this.
screens.why5: My pick, 'People I know by name', is shown as I chose it, and nothing about the study's meaning is changed.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is at the top, but its number '4 counted' names only Frequency when Importance and Current solution are short too, and it never says that 5 were needed or why only 4 of my 7 supers were counted.
screens.why_b2: The tally of 1 holding and 3 too few reads at once, and Prevalence's '6 of 7 · bar 6 of 7' is plain, but the three short cards show '4 counted · 5 needed' with no bar, so I can't see where they were heading.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence, Frequency, Importance and Current solution are my four beliefs nearly word for word, and the line under the title is my launch post, though 'loged' is a typo in my own belief.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do with three beliefs I can't call, whether to send the study to more superintendents, how many more, or whether to read the Prevalence result as enough to go on.
screens.why_b5: n=7 and the counts are shown honestly, but my 'spend hours every day on documents' sits under the title like a finding on a page where Importance and Current solution haven't been shown at all.
screens.instead: Too few to call: only 4 of 7 supers could be counted on Frequency, Importance and Current solution (5 needed for each), and nearly all logged last week; send it to at least 3 more superintendents before you read whether the log is one of their worst difficulties.

screens.why_b1: "Holding up" sits right beside 6 of 7 said yes against a bar of 6 of 7, so I know it held and by exactly what number.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 7 people, 6 for and 1 against, with the marker at 6 on a 0 to 7 axis, so what is counted, over how many and where my bar sits are plain at once.
screens.why_b3: The name and "At least 8 in 10" are mine, but "loged their site walk photos and notes" is misspelt and is the circumstance every super is in, not my problem of typing up the daily log after the walks; the gate asks the same thing, so I recognise the study but not quite my belief.
screens.why_b4: "How often, and whether it matters, are the next two cards" sends me on, but it does not say what a yes from 6 of 7 means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: The small group is said plainly ("a lean, not a call"), but "Holding up" on a gate that asks whether supers logged their photos at all, which nearly every working super does, softly overstates how common my problem is; the stray "— the most recent time it happened" after a yes/no question also reads oddly.
screens.instead: At least 8 in 10 construction superintendents on commercial jobs typed up the daily log after their site walks in the last 5 working days. Holding up: 6 of 7 said yes, exactly at your bar of 6, a lean from a small group. Asked: "In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks?"

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside its number, 4 counted with 5 needed, so I know why no verdict is given.
screens.why_b2: The axis (working days out of 5) and the median at 5 read at once, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5 (at least 2 in 3)' made me stop and work out whether 4 of 5 means people or days, and the 0 tick is an answer nobody could give.
screens.why_b3: It is my range of 4 to 5 working days out of 5, said about site walk photos and notes in my own trade's words, though the trailing 'the most recent time it happened' on the question doesn't fit a five-day count.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that all 4 counted are already for me and that one more counted superintendent settles it either way.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and Hank and Luis are set apart with their reasons, so nothing claims more than six answers carry.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 counted log on 4 or 5 days out of 5 (middle answer 5); one more counted superintendent and this holds whatever they say, so get one more answer before you lean on it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, 4 counted with 5 needed, and the So line repeats both.
screens.why_b2: I can see the bars count 8 picks over 4 people, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' needs a second look to square with 'at least 2 in 3', and the bars count picks while the bar counts people.
screens.why_b3: The card is titled Importance and the belief line is word for word the one I checked, with 'Logging the day's work' as my item; only the asked line's doubled 'last last 5 working days' reads off.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted answer decides this, or that the two against both put schedule and subs ahead of the log.
screens.why_b5: The count line calls a 2-for, 2-against split 'a lean, not a call' when there is no lean either way, a soft overstatement next to an otherwise honest small n.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put logging in their two and 2 put the schedule and subs first; one more answer decides it, and you need 4 of 5 to hold. (And ask 'Think of the last 5 working days on site'.)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, 4 counted and 5 needed, so I know why there is no call yet.
screens.why_b2: The bars and my line under 'Done in the trailer in under an hour' read at once, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with a ghost cell took a second look, since next to '4 counted' I first read it as a count rather than the bar for a group of five.
screens.why_b3: The card is titled Current solution, and the belief and the rung 'Done in the trailer in under an hour' are word for word what I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is a generic line: it does not say that 3 of my 4 already fell short, or that one more counted answer from a super would decide it.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible throughout, the two people not counted are named with reasons, and 'a lean, not a call' keeps 3 of 4 from being dressed up as a result.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted fell short of 'Done in the trailer in under an hour'; one more counted super decides it, so send the study to one more superintendent.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Too few to call' sits right on top with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' beside it, so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: The box is named Importance and the belief line is word for word the one I checked about logging being one of the two things supers would most like made easier.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more super counted, but the screen never says to send the study to more supers or what two against out of four would mean for my pitch if it held.
screens.why_b5: The count stays visible at every level (4 counted, 2 against, 2 asked, a group of 2) and nothing is called a finding on that base.
screens.why_b6: I didn't type that the schedule and subs not showing up beat the log for my supers, or that one already finishes her log on the tablet before the gate and another lets it wait till morning; that tells me the log is a deferrable chore, not the burning pain I pitched.
screens.instead: Say plainly: 2 of 4 put schedule and subs above the log, so this is too early to call; send to at least one more super before leaning on importance. Also say why Current solution has no box here.

screens.why1: As the first screen it makes sense to check that my jobs run on Procore or ACC before asking me anything about daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms I use every day, and 'any job you run now' is how I'd say it.
screens.why3: I know which platform each of my jobs is on, so I can answer straight away.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it with no gap or overlap, and a screener needs no escape.
screens.why5: It names only the platforms my GC uses and gives away nothing about anybody's product.
screens.why6: It's short and easy to hear, but 'I'll read 2 options. Yes; or No.' is clunky for a yes-or-no when the screener's spoken form should just end 'Yes or no.'
screens.instead: Is any job you run now on Procore or ACC? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking if my job runs on Procore or ACC, asking about my last few days of logging is the obvious next thing.
screens.why2: Site walk photos and notes, daily log -- that's how I talk, I'd answer it on one read.
screens.why3: I know exactly whether I logged my walk photos and notes this week; I do it every day.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, but every super I know says Yes to this every working day, so No is there in name only; the chips also sit on the gate screen though they belong to the story box after a Yes.
screens.why5: Nothing of a product reaches me, but the question has slid from the hassle of typing it all up afterwards to just doing the log, which is a different thing.
screens.why6: Short, one question, 'Yes or no' -- easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: The gate asks the circumstance every superintendent is in, logging site-walk photos and notes, not the problem counted, so everyone says Yes, No has nobody, and 'at least 8 in 10' can never be refuted -- the card's own bad example.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to logging my walk photos and notes this week, asking on how many days is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Site walks, photos, notes and the log are how I talk about my day, and I can answer it in one read.
screens.why3: I know which days this week I got my photos and notes into the daily log in Procore and which days I let them slide.
screens.why4: One button per working day from 1 to 5 covers every honest answer, with no zero I couldn't pick after saying yes, and 'I can't recall' sits apart as the only escape.
screens.why5: Nothing about anyone's product or plan comes through; it is just my own week on site.
screens.why6: Heard once, it is one short question with 'a number from 1 to 5' and the escape said last, easy to answer on the phone.
screens.why7: Every option is a count of working days in the window, the unit is said once, the buttons run 1 to 5 with no 0 or bands, logging is a single act on a given day in the simple past, and the one escape 'I can't recall' is there as the card requires.

screens.why1: Right after asking how many days I logged my walk photos and notes, it makes sense to ask where that sits next to the other headaches on my job.
screens.why2: "Think of your last last 5 working days on site" trips me up with the doubled "last", and it reads clumsily even though every option is in words I use.
screens.why3: Subs, RFIs, submittals, the daily log, schedule and safety are all things I deal with myself every week.
screens.why4: The options are real, but "keeping the job on schedule" swallows "getting subs to show up and finish", since subs not showing is most of why we slip.
screens.why5: Nothing about an app, Procore uploads or any product shows; it reads like a plain question about my week.
screens.why6: The five options say fine as a list, but "last last 5 working days" is a stumble the AI says aloud and a listener will notice.
screens.why7: The measure is one ("made easier"), the own item is present and not first, there are four rivals and None of these is at the first ask, but the rivals drift from the end-of-day logging moment to whole-job worries, with "keeping the job on schedule" close to the whole job and overlapping the subs row.
screens.instead: Think of the last 5 working days on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Getting subs to show up and finish · Chasing RFIs and submittals · Logging the day's photos and notes · Writing up delays and changes for the owner · Getting the punch list closed out · None of these

screens.why1: After asking which part of the day I'd most like made easier, asking how my last daily log actually went is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Daily log, trailer, the walk: that's how I talk about my day, and I'd get it on first hearing.
screens.why3: I write the log every day, so I know exactly how the last one went.
screens.why4: The trailer is on site, so the first two overlap, and there's a gap between under an hour and a couple of hours where a lot of my days land.
screens.why5: Nothing about an app or anybody's product reaches me; it's just about my log.
screens.why6: One question, five short options I can hold, and one escape said last.
screens.why7: The order is right, with two working rungs above the line and a real failure last, but the rungs mix where it got done with how long it took, and since my assistant super or project engineer could have done the log, the escape should be someone else did it rather than I can't recall.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did getting the photos and notes in take? Done before I left the walk; under an hour; one to two hours; more than two hours, or finished the next morning; never got done properly. Or say someone else did it.
